newsitem.title: USA: US Labor's Abraham - poll workers affected jobs gain.
newsitem.headline: US Labor's Abraham - poll workers affected jobs gain.

text.p: Calculations related to poll workers in the 1996 elections caused volatility in a component of the November and December employment reports, and that component would be one to keep an eye on in January, Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Katharine Abraham said Friday.

"The only number I might caution you about in the (employment) report is the number for state and local government non-education employment," she told reporters after testifying before the Joint Economic Committee.

"That number whipped down in November and then whipped back up this month, but that was really just an issue related to a seasonal adjustment issue related to a change in the pattern of employment for poll workers," she said.
Abraham said apparently a larger number of poll workers than in the previous year were treated by the state and local governments as contract workers rather than payroll employees.
About 25,000 of the 262,000 increase in December jobs was related to this seasonal adjustment "quirk," she said.
